newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee ends weaker but choppy NY sets pace.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee ends weaker but choppy NY sets pace.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures closed weaker across the board at the end of the week but most attention was centred on the volatile session in New York, market sources said on Friday.
London followed New York lower after sell stops on July arabicas were triggered at 200 cents/lb and then attacked by locals and speculators.

"New York broke through 200 and that's the story of the day," said one trader, adding that London had seen a usual scenario of early industry buying being offset by later U.S. commission house and fund selling.
London volume stayed on the lighter side, with the lower liquidity deterring larger-scale players.
"It's difficult to do anything in size at the moment because nobody here is doing anything," the trader said.
At the close July robustas stood down $10 at $1,755 with September down $10 at $1,785. Volume was 4,995 lots.
July is still hovering in the middle of a chart gap left between the June 10 low of $1,820 and the next day's high of $1,740. Resistance was seen at the gap's $1,720 with support near $1,600.
Traders said investors would be reluctant to set any new positions before the U.S. Department of Agriculture's (USDA) crop estimates, due after the New York close.
Early Brazilian trade estimates have put next season's crop at anywhere from 18 to 25 million 60-kg bags, after this year's yield of at least 27 million.
But some traders have said they expect the USDA 1997/98 Brazil forecast to surpass the local estimates, and have floated a figure of 27 million bags.
The Green Coffee Association of New York will release its May inventory data on Monday at 1900 GMT.
Aggressive shipments by producers are expected to increase stocks by some 150,000-250,000 bags in May, although some estimates are even higher.
Back in Brazil, local meteorologist Somar said the coffee regions should see rainy, cloudy weather over the coming days with seasonal temperatures and no damaging cold in sight.
A cold front which has arrived in the south of the country should bring showers to coffee regions over the weekend which will hit the harvest, Somar said.
